Expert 1 here — the classifier that reads the structured panel and nothing else. My bid:

SUGGESTION: BIOPSY   p(biopsy) = 0.79
  uncertainty  +/- 0.07 epistemic (95% band 0.66-0.92); among patients I cannot tell apart the outcome was 0.74 of 1.00 mixed
  reliability  HIGH ('firm' tier) — out-of-fold it was right 88% of the time over the 33 labelled cases in this tier

What moved me most, across the labelled series: prior positive biopsy, PI-RADS >= 4, no prior biopsy, pmhx_hypercholesterolaemia, suspicious DRE, number of comorbidities. I read 39 variables, all
from the panel — nothing from the mpMRI prose, the PSA trajectory, the previous notes or the
laboratory. Out-of-fold over 91 labelled cases: AUC 0.758, balanced
accuracy 0.625.

The final call is the chair's.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-EAU
interventions.who: EAU guideline specialist; speaks only from the guideline text he retrieved
interventions.body:
GUIDELINE
The EAU guidelines link PI-RADS scores to the indication for biopsy, noting that a PI-RADS score of 3 or higher is used to trigger a biopsy. The guideline also suggests that MRI-directed US-guided prostate biopsy is now the standard of care.

WHAT THE EXPERTS' BIDS DO NOT SETTLE
Expert 1's suggestion of biopsy is not decisive because the guideline focuses on the PI-RADS score, which is present, but the guideline does not provide a definitive threshold for action based solely on the score in isolation. The cohort criterion suggests that the decision hinges on whether the mpMRI shows a PI-RADS 3 or higher lesion, which is a finding that must be confirmed by the opened radiology report.

WHAT WE STILL NEED
The panel already contains the following known facts:
*   PI-RADS: 5 (This is above the threshold of 3 mentioned in the guideline).
*   Prior biopsy status: None (This is a key factor in the guideline's context).
*   PSA: 5.9 ng/mL (This is a known value, but the guideline does not provide a specific PSA threshold for this decision).
*   PSA density: 0.199 ng/mL² (This value is close to the 0.20 ng/mL/cc mentioned in the guideline's context).
*   Prostate volume: 29.71 mL.
*   DRE finding: Normal.
*   Months since last PSA: 1.
*   csPCa probability: 0.84285355.
*   The grade of the prior biopsy is "None," which is a known fact relevant to the guideline's context.

FOR sampling this patient now

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-PSA
interventions.who: Expert 2, PSA projector; the trajectory behind the headline PSA, with a conformal band
interventions.body:
Expert 2 here — the PSA projector. I read only the serial PSA the registrar opened.

TRAJECTORY: RISING (borderline). Last value 5.90 ng/mL over 3 points spanning 33 months; velocity +0.61 ng/mL per year; doubling time about 69 months.
PROJECTION at 6 months: 7.9 ng/mL, conformal 95% band 2.3-27.7.

Read the band before the point: it is wide by construction, and I only call a direction when the whole
band clears the last value. This does not vote on the biopsy — a rising PSA in a man with a known
diagnosis is the disease behaving as known — it tells the chair how fast the number is moving.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-FUSION
interventions.who: Expert 3, Extra-Trees on panel + laboratory + MRI prose; speaks only on documents that were opened
interventions.body:
Expert 3 here — the fusion classifier. I read the panel, the mpMRI report — the laboratory panel was not opened, so that block is imputed and my band is wider for it; nothing from the previous notes or the PSA series.

SUGGESTION: BIOPSY   p(biopsy) = 0.82
  uncertainty  +/- 0.06 epistemic (95% band 0.71-0.93), of which 0.00 comes from values that had to be imputed
  reliability  HIGH ('firm' tier) — out-of-fold it was right 89% of the time over the 37 labelled cases in this tier

What moved me most across the labelled series: prior positive biopsy, no prior biopsy, free PSA < 15%, DWI restriction in the report, lesion >= 15 mm in the report, suspicious DRE. Out-of-fold AUC 0.794. I am the only expert that has read the report's wording, and I still cannot see the prior grade or the
surveillance history: those are in the notes, and the registrar has to carry them.

data.gist: Expert 3 suggests BIOPSY, p=0.82 +/- 0.06, HIGH reliability (firm, fusion_nolab)

interventions.body:
SUFFICIENCY
The documents opened—radiology_report, psa_trend, and previous_notes—directly address both open questions. The radiology report provided the size and zone of the lesion, and the previous notes detailed the management context regarding prior biopsy status and surveillance.

ALIGNMENT WITH THE PANEL
The retrieved evidence strongly aligns with the PANEL-PROTOCOL's answer of BIOPSY, as the PI-RADS 5 finding (from the radiology report) satisfies the cohort criterion (pirads_ge_3).

THE OPEN QUESTIONS, ONE BY ONE
Q1. What is the size and zone of the lesion described in the radiology report? Answered by the registrar: "a 'discrete hypointense focus located posteriorly in the mid-gland left peripheral zone, spanning 12 x 9 x 10 mm.'"

Driven by this trend and mild urinary complaints, clinicians ordered an mpMRI and initiated a urology referral. Tamsulosin remained part of the regimen for symptom management."

WHAT CARRIES WEIGHT, AND WHY
The PI-RADS 5 score from the radiology report is the most decisive variable, as it directly triggers the cohort criterion which the PANEL-PROTOCOL confirms. The PSA trend showing an upward trajectory further supports the clinical concern.

MY SUGGESTION TO THE CHAIR
I suggest proceeding with a biopsy, as the retrieved evidence fully satisfies the criteria established by the panel protocol.

VERDICT: ready | SUGGEST: biopsy | MISSING: none
